catalog_quote: 3.5 Stress. Stress in Mali is not contrastive. There are no minimal pairs in the language distinguished by stress. Note that the phonological word does not map consistently onto the lexical word in Mali, making statements about lexical prominence problematic. Mali seems to have a basic pattern similar to the one reported for many Oceanic languages in which stress tends to be fixed on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word. However, like Stanton (2007:84–85), in her study of Ura, I found quite a few exceptions to this tendency. Instrumental analysis shows that prominence is marked with an increase in intensity, and possibly duration and vowel quality. ... In fluent speech there may be a single pitch contour for the predicate, and for individual noun or prepositional phrases within the clause. ... sweep_summary: Only one sweep item for Mali (mali1284): Stebbins 2004, 'Mali Baining perspectives on language and culture stress', IJSL 169:161-175 (DOI 10.1515/ijsl.2004.039). It is a sociolinguistic paper (Glottolog socling; IJSL 'Small Languages and Small Language Communities' column; the 2011 grammar cites it only for accommodative language use and Tok Pisin expansion) -- 'stress' in the title is cultural pressure, not word stress. It is closed access with no repository copy (Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex/Unpaywall all closed; De Gruyter Brill blocks non-browser clients; the Wayback snapshot 404s), so it was not read; priority none. No new first-hand stress statement was found. The catalog's deciding source, Stebbins 2011 Mali (Baining) grammar (PL 623), already on file at, was re-read at sec. 3.5 'Stress' pp. 33-34 (text-layer lines 2135-2163), ch. 3 intro (lines 1409-1413) and sec. 3.6 (lines 2167-2168): the catalog quote is verbatim ('Stress in Mali is not contrastive... Mali seems to have a basic pattern... stress tends to be fixed on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word. However, like Stanton (2007:84-85)... I found quite a few exceptions to this tendency... Given its low salience in the language, stress has not been marked in this description'), and the 'undetermined' coding stands; the sweep neither refines nor contradicts it.

audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim at the stated locators in the held open-access grammar. The coding 'undetermined' with a prose rule recording a hedged penultimate tendency on the phonological word, pervasive exceptions, and the author's own doubt that prominence is lexical at all, faithfully reflects Stebbins's sec. 3.5 and ch.3 intro; the author explicitly leaves stress unmarked for low salience. No later or more specialised phonological/instrumental study of Mali exists in Glottolog, Semantic Scholar or Crossref; related-language work (Stanton 2007 on Ura, Tabain & Hellwig 2022 JIPA on Qaqet) does not bear on this languoid's record. Nothing to fetch; no recode warranted.
